meta.name: Generate branded prospect websites with Claude, Jina, GitHub Pages, and Gmail

parameters.content:
## AI Company Website Generator

Give it a company name, their website, and an email, and it builds them a brand new site on its own. It scrapes their real site with Jina, has Claude pull out their actual colors, copy, and content, then has Claude write a full animated HTML page that matches their brand. The finished site gets pushed live to GitHub Pages and the link gets emailed out.

Uses: n8n Form Trigger, Jina AI Reader, Claude Haiku, Claude Sonnet, GitHub API, Gmail.

You'll need an Anthropic API key, a Jina API key (set as the JINA_API_KEY environment variable), a GitHub credential with write access to your Pages repo, and Gmail credentials.

Good for sales teams who want to send a prospect a live mockup of their own site as a personalized lead magnet.

### Trigger

A simple form collects the company name, their website, and an email address. Everything downstream pulls from this one submission.

### Scraping the site

Jina reads the homepage first. Then Code: Scrape All Pages finds the real internal links on it, skips the junk like logins, legal pages, and social links, and pulls in up to twenty more pages so the AI has the full picture, not just the homepage.

### Extracting the brand

Claude Haiku reads through everything scraped and pulls out only what's actually there: headlines, colors, services, testimonials, team bios, whatever exists. Nothing gets invented. Code4 parses that response and passes it along.

### Generating the site

Claude Sonnet takes that extracted content and writes a full animated HTML page styled to match the brand, using only the sections that had real content. Code: Extract HTML then cleans up the response so it's ready to publish.

### Publishing to GitHub Pages

The HTML gets encoded and pushed to a folder named after the company. If a site already exists there, the If node catches it and routes to Edit a file to update it instead of failing. Merge2 brings both paths back together.

### Sending it off

Generate Website URL builds the final live link. Wait2 gives GitHub Pages a moment to finish deploying, then the email goes out with the site link.

parameters.subject: =Your website is ready

parameters.jsonBody:
={ 
  "model": "claude-sonnet-4-6",
  "max_tokens": 16000,
  "messages": [
    {
      "role": "user",
      "content": {{ JSON.stringify("You are building an automated website generation system for a B2B cold email agency. The goal is to generate high-quality, visually impressive, fully clickable single-file HTML websites for prospect companies at scale. Each website will be used as a lead magnet in cold outreach emails.

Here is exactly what you need to build:

---

WHAT THIS SYSTEM DOES

Given a company name, their website URL, and scraped content, generate a complete single-file HTML website that:

1. Visually mirrors the prospect's brand (colors, tone, industry feel)
2. Has smooth scroll animations, parallax effects, and hover interactions
3. Includes all their real navigation links and sub-links (clickable, pointing to their actual live URLs)
4. Sections only appear if real content was found for them
5. Outputs a complete, production-ready HTML file with all CSS and JavaScript embedded

---

EXTRACTED CONTENT:

" + JSON.stringify($json.ai) + "

---

STEP 3: GENERATE THE WEBSITE

Generate a single complete HTML file. Every section must have smooth entrance animations triggered on scroll (use IntersectionObserver). The site must feel alive and premium.

DESIGN REQUIREMENTS:

Typography:
- Import DM Sans from Google Fonts
- Hero headline: 56px to 72px, font-weight 700, letter-spacing -2px
- Section headings: 40px to 48px, font-weight 700
- Body text: 16px to 18px, line-height 1.7
- Use the company's actual brand colors from primary_color and secondary_color in the extracted content

Navigation:
- Sticky nav that becomes solid on scroll (starts transparent)
- Logo (company name text) on the left
- All nav_links rendered as real clickable anchor tags pointing to their actual live URLs
- Nav links open in a new tab (target='_blank' rel='noopener noreferrer')
- CTA button on the right

Hero Section (always include):
- Full viewport height
- Large headline with the company's actual headline
- Subtext beneath it
- CTA button linking to hero.cta_url
- Subtle background animation (floating gradient orbs using CSS keyframes)

Stats Bar (if stats.exists is true):
- Horizontal display of stat values and labels
- Numbers animate from 0 to their value when scrolled into view using IntersectionObserver and requestAnimationFrame

Services / Features (if services.exists or features.exists is true):
- Card grid with hover effects (card lifts on hover with box-shadow transition)
- Each card has title and description

Process (if process.exists is true):
- Numbered steps in a horizontal or vertical layout
- Step numbers are large and styled with the brand color

Portfolio / Work (if portfolio.exists is true):
- Card grid
- If a URL exists for a portfolio item, make the card clickable (open in new tab)

Testimonials (if testimonials.exists is true):
- Quote cards with italic quote text, author name and title
- Subtle border or background tint

Team (if team.exists is true):
- Grid of team member cards
- Circular photo if photo URL exists, otherwise initials fallback in a colored circle
- Name, title, bio

About (if about.exists is true):
- Clean text section with the company's actual story

Clients (if clients.exists is true):
- Horizontal display of client names

FAQ (if faq.exists is true):
- Accordion style (click to expand/collapse each item)
- Smooth height transition using max-height

CTA Section:
- Dark background (use the extracted primary color darkened)
- Large headline, subtext, button
- Button links to cta.button_url

Footer:
- Dark background
- Company name and tagline
- All footer.links rendered as real clickable anchors pointing to their actual live URLs
- Copyright line with current year

ANIMATION REQUIREMENTS:

All section content fades in and slides up on scroll:

.animate { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(30px); transition: opacity 0.6s ease, transform 0.6s ease; }
.animate.visible { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0); }

const observer = new IntersectionObserver((entries) => { entries.forEach(entry => { if (entry.isIntersecting) { entry.target.classList.add('visible'); } }); }, { threshold: 0.1 }); document.querySelectorAll('.animate').forEach(el => observer.observe(el));

Nav scroll behavior:
window.addEventListener('scroll', () => { const nav = document.querySelector('nav'); if (window.scrollY > 50) { nav.classList.add('scrolled'); } else { nav.classList.remove('scrolled'); } });

Stat counter animation:
function animateCounter(el, target) { let start = 0; const duration = 1500; const startTime = performance.now(); function update(currentTime) { const elapsed = currentTime - startTime; const progress = Math.min(elapsed / duration, 1); const value = Math.floor(progress * target); el.textContent = value.toLocaleString() + (el.dataset.suffix || ''); if (progress < 1) requestAnimationFrame(update); } requestAnimationFrame(update); }

FAQ accordion:
Use max-height transition for smooth open/close. No libraries.

STEP 4: OUTPUT

Output only the complete HTML file. Nothing else. No explanation. No backticks. No markdown. The very first character must be <!DOCTYPE html>.

The file must be completely self-contained. No external dependencies except Google Fonts (loaded via link tag in head) and no external JavaScript libraries.

QUALITY BAR:
- Every nav link points to a real URL from the company's site, opens in new tab
- Every footer link points to a real URL
- All portfolio items with URLs are clickable
- Stats counter animation works
- FAQ accordion works without any library
- Site looks premium on desktop
- No section appears with placeholder or invented content
- Color scheme matches the company's actual brand

COMPANY: " + $('On form submission').first().json['Company Name'] + "
WEBSITE: " + $('On form submission').first().json['Company Website']) }}
    }
  ]
}
